chunks.sanskrit: saḥ jayati śivaḥ ekaḥ spandavān svapratiṣṭhaḥ | yaḥ antarvaktram rasayati
chunks.l1:
## sand-p01-v01 (1)
He / is-victorious / Śiva / alone / possessing-spanda / self-established / who / inner-face / makes-taste // sand-p01
chunks.l2: He alone — Śiva, possessing spanda, self-established — who makes the inner face taste.
chunks.l3: He alone conquers — Śiva, throbbing, self-established — who savors the inner face.
chunks.l4:
He alone conquers — Śiva, throbbing, self-standing,
tasting the inward face — conquers alone.
chunks.c1:
## sand-p01-v01 — C1

*Rasa: adbhuta (wonder at Śiva's spanda) with śānta (tranquility of self-established nature) — The sthāyibhāva is wonder (vismaya) at Śiva's unmeasured greatness (akalitamahimā), resolving into tranquility (śama) — the ocean unmoved by world-waves. Application: Abhinava does not explicitly name a rasa for this verse; the adbhuta/śānta reading is mine.*
chunks.argmap:
## sand-p01-v01 — argument map

He alone, Śiva, is victorious (sa jayati śiva ekaḥ): alone = non-dual. Possessing spanda, self-established (spandavān svapratiṣṭhaḥ). Who makes the inner face taste (antarvaktra rasayati): I-consciousness tasteable.

chunks.l1:
## sand-p01-v02 (2)
is-victorious / this / hero / lord-of-the-Kula // sand-p01
chunks.l2: This hero, lord of the Kula — victorious.
chunks.l3: Victorious is this hero, the Kula’s lord.
chunks.l4:
Victorious, this hero — the Kula's lord —
victorious.
chunks.argmap:
## sand-p01-v02 — argument map

This hero, lord of the Kula, is victorious (jayatyeṣa vīraḥ kulendraḥ).
